answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost.
